title: ML Numerics and Loss Curves
prompt:
Implement four NumPy numerical utilities on finite real-valued inputs.

`stable_softmax(logits)` returns an array of the same shape, normalizing the final axis. Support one-dimensional and batched inputs; shift logits before exponentiation to avoid overflow.

`standardize_columns(X)` takes a nonempty 2-D feature matrix and returns `(X - column_mean) / column_std`, using population standard deviation (`ddof=0`). Reject a constant column instead of adding an epsilon.

`ridge_gradient(X, y, weights, bias, l2)` returns `(weight_gradient, bias_gradient)` for the explicit objective `mean((X @ weights + bias - y)**2) + l2 * sum(weights**2)`, with one-dimensional y and weights. There is no one-half factor. Regularize only weights, not bias.

`LossCurve(values)` accepts a nonempty one-dimensional loss sequence. `moving_average(window)` returns the `len(values)-window+1` means of full consecutive windows. `best_window(window)` returns the earliest start index of the smallest moving average. Reject nonpositive or oversized integer windows; `assert` or `ValueError` is sufficient. Use vectorized NumPy, do not mutate input arrays, and keep loss-curve methods linear in the sequence length. These independent helpers form a local preparation exercise, not a recovered four-part interview prompt.

example.reasoning: The window starting at index 1 has mean 2.0, the smallest of the three windows.
